meta.title: Property tax exemption routes and assessor track records by county and place
meta.method: Curated, not a feed. Routes rest on the quoted statute text below. Assessor history is read from each county assessor's public record, one account at a time, and every item quotes the record line it rests on. An exempt share is recorded only where the record shows it. A county whose records were not read has status not_researched. A blank means not checked, never no history.
meta.rule: Every deal assessment weighs a housing authority lease or ownership interest as the property tax route, and reads the local assessor's history on housing exemptions.
known_gaps: Five geographies so far: La Plata, Delta and Morgan counties, Bayfield and Durango.
The assessor record shows the result, not the statute or the application; which exemption route each project used is not recorded.
Payment in lieu of tax (PILOT) agreements are not on assessor records and are left blank until a public agreement is read.
Named people to call are kept on the member site, not in this public file.

verification.by: colorado.public.law (unofficial reproduction of the official 2024 C.R.S.)

statutes.quote: All property of an authority is exempt from all local and municipal taxes. Bonds, notes, debentures, and other evidences of indebtedness of an authority are declared to be issued for a public purpose and to be public instruments, and, together with interest thereon, are exempt from taxes. All property leased to an authority for the purposes of a project is also exempt from taxation, as is the income derived from the authority by the lessor under the lease.

verification.by: colorado.public.law (unofficial reproduction of the official 2024 C.R.S.)

statutes.quote: A project that is owned by, leased to, or under construction by an entity that is wholly owned by an authority, an entity in which an authority has an ownership interest, or an entity in which an entity wholly owned by an authority or of which an authority is the sole member has an ownership interest is exempt from both property tax and, during construction, from the payment of sales tax and use tax to the state or any county, city and county, municipality, or other political subdivision of the state in proportion to the percentage of the project that is for occupancy by persons of low income.
